extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of literary biography and travel writing (general educated readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative language for judging travel writing and related biographical prose, illustrated by commentary on Boswell's Journal to the Hebrides and Johnson's Journey. Emphasises descriptive accuracy, style, character-revelation, and reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of description
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay explicitly praises Boswell: 'No better book of travels in Scotland has ever been written than Boswell's Journal.' The text credits the book's accuracy and notes that Johnson read the journal day by day during its preparation, giving 'additional value from the perfect veracity of its contents.' Use factual precision and verifiable detail as a criterion for good travel writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eye for scenes and dramatic effects
rubrics_metrics.description: his eye for scenes and dramatic effects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlighted as a distinguishing quality of Boswell's Journal. Evaluate whether the writer notices and renders striking scenes and arranges incidents for dramatic effect (e.g., memorable descriptions such as Iona).

rubrics_metrics.name: Veracity / fidelity to events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats veracity as an explicit virtue (Johnson reading the journal while Boswell prepared it is cited as bolstering veracity). Assess whether the account is truthful, avoids invention, and preserves the events as experienced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic opening and grouping of characters
rubrics_metrics.description: the artistic opening, and the grouping of the characters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'artistic opening' and thoughtful staging/grouping of cast are named as formal devices that elevate the book. Judge openings for their ability to set tone and group characters for sustained interest and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wealth of archaeological and historical information
rubrics_metrics.description: the wealth of archaeological and historical information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inclusion of archaeological and historical material is presented as adding value to the travel narrative. Evaluate the extent, relevance, and accuracy of background information that situates scenes historically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tripping style and sustained interest
rubrics_metrics.description: the tripping style and sustained interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style that is lively ('tripping') and keeps the reader engaged from 'start to finish' is praised. Use measures like absence of dull pages, pacing, and sustained narrative interest to judge success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary polish / quality of prose
rubrics_metrics.description: the literary polish is ... of a higher kind than is seen in the Life
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare levels of polish, control of language, and refinement of prose. The essay explicitly contrasts Boswell's polish favourably against Johnson's Life; judge sentences, tone, and finish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of dullness / continuous engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: From start to finish there is not a dull page
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of boredom or dead stretches is noted as a key indicator of success. Assess chapters/sections for engagement and narrative energy throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reticence / discretion (handling sensitive material)
rubrics_metrics.description: There had been grave indiscretions, lack of reticence, and other faults in the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay flags 'indiscretions' and lack of reticence as faults; editing decisions (e.g., leaves 'torn out' for second edition) and responses to criticism are relevant. Judge whether an author shows appropriate discretion about private or delicate matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character revelation / faithful portrayal of persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Read in the original, as a revelation of the writer's character, the very reverse is the impression; he is ... presented not in any ludicrous light but rather in a good-humoured and fussy way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the work reveals the personalities of its subjects faithfully and with nuance (avoiding caricature), and whether it contributes to an accurate, humane portrait rather than mockery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companionly behaviour and authorial empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: Boswell's attention to the old man smoothed all difficulties,--'looking on the tour as a co-partnership between Dr Johnson and myself,' he did his part faithfully, dancing reels, singing songs, and airing the scraps of Gaelic he picked up
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a criterion for travel-writing that involves others, evaluate the author's attentiveness to companions and how that social conduct shapes the narrative: empathy, participation, and smoothing of difficulties enhance the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive fame / memorable passages
rubrics_metrics.description: One passage from it has become famous,--his description of Iona.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A work's ability to produce memorable, oft-quoted passages (quotability) is cited as a mark of descriptive power. Note passages likely to endure or enter common reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception and influence (editions, translations, public response)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boswell's appeared in September, 1785; and by December 20 the issue was exhausted, a third followed ... and the next year saw a German translation issued at Lubeck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contemporary reception—speed of sell-out, multiple editions, translations, and public controversies—serves as evidence of a work's impact and success. Consider reviews, controversies, and subsequent influence when judging importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between anecdote and larger historical/political context
rubrics_metrics.description: The artistic opening, and the grouping of the characters, together with the wealth of archaeological and historical information ... all render this book ... a masterpiece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the narrative balances anecdotal, personal material with broader historical, archaeological, or political context to create a satisfying, informative whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace and lightness of touch in prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Johnson's account ... is written with a lighter touch and grace than is to be found in his early works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tone and manner: 'light touch' and 'grace' are praised as qualities that can make descriptive prose more effective. Assess whether the prose handles subjects with appropriate elegance and levity where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral or ethical stance expressed by the author
rubrics_metrics.description: He fairly acknowledge[s] that I love drinking; that I have a constitutional inclination ... to conduct it in the most rational and agreeable manner is one of the great arts of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence and articulation of an author's moral or philosophical reflections (e.g., on drinking, piety, reticence) function as evaluative material; judge how such stances affect readers' response and the work's seriousness or frivolity.
